title: Erdős Problem #1142: Primes of the form n − 2^k
description: Are there infinitely many n (or any n > 105) such that n − 2^k is prime for all 1 < 2^k < n?

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős Problem #1142 concerns primes of the form n − 2^k. This problem remains OPEN.

Known results include: - The only known values are n ∈ {4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105} (OEIS A039669). - Mientka & Weitzenkamp (1969) verified no other n ≤ 2^44 satisfy this. - Vaughan (1973) showed the count of such n up to N is extremely sparse. - Erdős conjectured the number of 1 < 2^k < n for which n − 2^k is prime

This problem is catalogued at erdosproblems.com/1142.
